previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of spinal gunshot wound, neurogenic bladder, and chronic indwelling catheter was admitted for left-sided back pain, fevers, and chills concerning for pyelonephritis. She also reported a productive cough and hoarseness. Initial labs showed leukocytosis, and urinalysis indicated infection. Blood cultures were negative. Urine culture grew ESBL-producing E. coli, resistant to most antibiotics but sensitive to nitrofurantoin, tobramycin, and meropenem. Given clinical improvement on initial therapy and resolution of fever, she was diagnosed with bacterial cystitis rather than pyelonephritis. She was transitioned to oral nitrofurantoin for outpatient treatment. A primary care appointment was arranged, and she was counseled on the benefits of a suprapubic catheter to reduce infection risk. She was also advised about the health risks of ongoing cocaine use. She improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics and obtain a follow-up urine culture.

new PCP but never followed up on this. For the past week, she 
reports that the left flank pain has been getting progressively 
worse and her appetite has decreased. She also reports 
subjective fevers although has not measured them.

In the ED, she was given Dilaudid and Benadryl for pain control. 
She was given nitrofurantoin given her last UCx sensitivities 
and the fact that she was discharged on this last time. Vital 
signs were stable (96.8, 92, 120/54, 100% RA). She was admitted 
for pain control as she stated the Dilaudid was not helping 
enough. On the floor, she reported excruciating pain but looked 
calm and not in distress.

Brief Hospital Course:
## left flank pain: patient reports this is consistent with 
prior pyelo episodes but she does not appear in any distress. 
Given resistant organisms isolated in urine last admission, 
concern for E. coli ESBL causing recurrent infection. However, 
she did not appear toxic, was not febrile, UA had several epis, 
repeat UCx with mixed flora, WBC decreasing, renal US with no 
evidence of pyleo or obstruction, so unlikely that this is truly 
pathogenic. Thus, she was not treated with antibiotics as we did 
not want to expose her to more Abx unnecessarily and breed 
further resistance in what may be colonizers. Her Foley catheter 
was changed on admission. She was given pain medications that 
were quickly tapered off during her hospitalization. CT scan was 
considered but given that eight CT scans of her abd/pelvis were 
done in a one year period (___), we held off on exposing 
her to more radiation as she looked clinically well. She 
underwent a renal US instead that showed no hydro, pyelo or 
obstruction.

## neurogenic bladder: suprapubic catheter was considered given 
recurrent infection; however, given her poor compliance with 
followup and unstable living situation, this was not recommended 
at this time as complications from infection of more permanent 
catheter could be worse than with Foley that is more easily 
changed.

## substance abuse: urine tox positive for cocaine, continued 
couselling against drug use  

## depression/anxiety: continued prozac
